title.en: The Past Perfect Continuous (I had been waiting)
title.es: El pasado perfecto continuo (I had been waiting)

text.en: The past perfect continuous is formed with had been + verb-ing: “I had been waiting”. It describes an action that began before a moment in the past and lasted up to that moment: “I had been waiting for two hours when the bus arrived.” It matches the Spanish “llevaba + gerundio”: “Llevaba dos horas esperando cuando llegó el camión.” There are always two points in the past: the other event (past simple) and the longer action that went on before it.
text.es: El pasado perfecto continuo se forma con had been + verbo-ing: «I had been waiting». Describe una acción que empezó antes de un momento del pasado y duró hasta ese momento: «I had been waiting for two hours when the bus arrived.» Equivale al «llevaba + gerundio» del español: «Llevaba dos horas esperando cuando llegó el camión.» Siempre hay dos puntos en el pasado: el otro hecho (pasado simple) y la acción más larga que duró antes.

rows: una acción larga hasta un momento del pasado
una acción en marcha en un momento del pasado
un resultado terminado antes de un momento del pasado
un hecho terminado en un momento del pasado
el punto de inicio (desde las seis)

text.en: Affirmative: had been + verb-ing, the same for every person. Negative: hadn’t been + verb-ing. Short form: I’d been waiting.
text.es: Afirmativa: had been + verbo-ing, igual para todas las personas. Negación: hadn’t been + verbo-ing. Forma corta: I’d been waiting.

examples.es: She had been working there for ten years.

tr.en: She had been working there for ten years.
tr.es: Llevaba diez años trabajando allí.

examples.es: He hadn't been working long when the boss arrived.

tr.en: He hadn't been working long when the boss arrived.
tr.es: No llevaba mucho tiempo trabajando cuando llegó el jefe.

text.en: Question: Had + subject + been + verb-ing. How long…? asks about the length: “How long had you been driving when the car stopped?”
text.es: Pregunta: Had + sujeto + been + verbo-ing. How long…? pregunta por la duración: «How long had you been driving when the car stopped?»

examples.es: How long had you been driving when the car stopped?

tr.en: How long had you been driving when the car stopped?
tr.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevabas manejando cuando se paró el carro?

examples.es: Had they been playing long when it started to rain?

tr.en: Had they been playing long when it started to rain?
tr.es: ¿Llevaban mucho tiempo jugando cuando empezó a llover?

text.en: An action lasting up to a point in the past, with a duration or a starting point: for + duration, since + starting point.
text.es: Una acción que duró hasta un punto del pasado, con una duración o un punto de inicio: for + duración, since + punto de inicio.

examples.es: We had been living there since 2015 when we moved away.

tr.en: We had been living there since 2015 when we moved away.
tr.es: Vivíamos allí desde 2015 cuando nos mudamos a otro lugar.

examples.es: They had been living in Puebla for ten years when she got the job.

tr.en: They had been living in Puebla for ten years when she got the job.
tr.es: Llevaban diez años viviendo en Puebla cuando ella consiguió el trabajo.

text.en: The process matters, not the number. When you give a number or a finished result, you need the simple past perfect: “By noon, she had written three reports.”
text.es: Importa el proceso, no el número. Si das un número o un resultado terminado, hace falta el pasado perfecto simple: «By noon, she had written three reports.»

examples.es: She had been writing reports all morning.

tr.en: She had been writing reports all morning.
tr.es: Llevaba toda la mañana escribiendo reportes.

examples.es: By noon, she had written three reports.

tr.en: By noon, she had written three reports.
tr.es: Para el mediodía, había escrito tres reportes.

text.en: The Spanish “estaba esperando desde ayer” is not “I was waiting since yesterday” in English. With since and for, time that lasts up to another point in the past needs the past perfect continuous: “I had been waiting since yesterday when you called.”
text.es: El «estaba esperando desde ayer» español no es «I was waiting since yesterday» en inglés. Con since y for, el tiempo que dura hasta otro punto del pasado necesita el pasado perfecto continuo: «I had been waiting since yesterday when you called.»

text.en: State verbs (know, like, love, want, have meaning own) take no -ing form here either: not “I had been knowing her”, but “I had known her for years”.
text.es: Los verbos de estado (know, like, love, want, have con el sentido de tener) tampoco llevan -ing aquí: no «I had been knowing her», sino «I had known her for years».

text.en: If the sentence describes an action going on at a single moment with no duration, the past continuous is enough: “I was watching TV when you called.” The sign of a long process up to that moment is for / since.
text.es: Si la oración describe una acción en marcha en un solo momento, sin duración, basta el pasado continuo: «I was watching TV when you called.» La señal de un proceso largo hasta ese momento es for / since.

speak.en: The past perfect continuous is «had been» plus the -ing form of the verb: «I had been waiting». It describes an action that began before a moment in the past and lasted up to it: «I had been waiting for two hours when the bus arrived». Before a duration comes «for», before a starting point «since». When you give a number or a finished result you need the simple past perfect: «By noon, she had written three reports». State verbs take no -ing form: «I had known her for years».
speak.es: El pasado perfecto continuo es «had been» más la forma -ing del verbo: «I had been waiting». Describe una acción que empezó antes de un momento del pasado y duró hasta él: «I had been waiting for two hours when the bus arrived». Antes de una duración va «for», antes de un punto de inicio «since». Si das un número o un resultado terminado, hace falta el pasado perfecto simple: «By noon, she had written three reports». Los verbos de estado no llevan -ing: «I had known her for years».

items.sentence: When the bus finally arrived, we ___ for two hours.

why.en: “For two hours” is the time before the bus arrived: had been waiting.
why.es: «For two hours» es el tiempo antes de que llegara el camión: had been waiting.

have been waiting.en: Have been waiting is the present perfect continuous, for time up to now, but the sentence refers to a point in the past (arrived).
have been waiting.es: Have been waiting es el presente perfecto continuo, para el tiempo hasta ahora, pero la oración se refiere a un punto del pasado (arrived).

will have been waiting.en: Will have been waiting marks time up to a future point; the sentence is in the past (arrived).
will have been waiting.es: Will have been waiting marca el tiempo hasta un punto futuro; la oración está en pasado (arrived).

examples: She had been waiting for an hour.
We had been waiting for a long time.

tr.en: When the bus finally arrived, we had been waiting for two hours.
tr.es: Cuando el camión finalmente llegó, habíamos estado esperando por dos horas.

items.sentence: By the time he called, I ___ since six o'clock.

why.en: “Since six o’clock” is a starting point before the call: had been working.
why.es: «Since six o’clock» es un punto de inicio antes de la llamada: had been working.

was working.en: Since does not go with the past continuous (not “was working since”); time lasting up to the call needs had been working.
was working.es: Since no va con el pasado continuo (no «was working since»); el tiempo que dura hasta la llamada necesita had been working.

have been working.en: Have been working belongs to the present; the sentence looks back from the moment of the call in the past.
have been working.es: Have been working pertenece al presente; la oración mira atrás desde el momento de la llamada en el pasado.

examples: He had been sleeping since noon.
They had been walking since morning.

tr.en: By the time he called, I had been working since six o'clock.
tr.es: Para cuando llamó, yo había estado trabajando desde las seis.

items.sentence: She ___ for two hours when I got there.

why.en: “When I got there” is a point in the past, and before it she waited for two hours: had been waiting.
why.es: «When I got there» es un punto del pasado, y antes esperó dos horas: had been waiting.

has been waiting.en: Has been waiting refers to the present; “when I got there” is a moment in the past.
has been waiting.es: Has been waiting se refiere al presente; «when I got there» es un momento del pasado.

is waiting.en: “Is waiting” is present; the sentence is in the past (got).
is waiting.es: «Is waiting» es presente; la oración está en pasado (got).

examples: He had been working for hours.
We had been talking for a long time.

tr.en: She had been waiting for two hours when I got there.
tr.es: Ella había estado esperando por dos horas cuando llegué ahí.

items.sentence: How long ___ you been driving when the car stopped?

why.en: For a duration up to a point in the past the question is How long had you been…?
why.es: Para una duración hasta un punto del pasado la pregunta es How long had you been…?

have.en: Have you been would ask about time up to now; the sentence refers to a point in the past (stopped).
have.es: Have you been preguntaría por el tiempo hasta ahora; la oración se refiere a un punto del pasado (stopped).

did.en: After did you need the base verb (How long did you drive…?); the structure “been driving” needs had.
did.es: Después de did hace falta el verbo base (How long did you drive…?); la estructura «been driving» necesita had.

examples: How long had she been waiting?
How long had they been living there?

tr.en: How long had you been driving when the car stopped?
tr.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo habías estado manejando cuando el carro se detuvo?

items.sentence: ___ they been playing long when it started to rain?

why.en: A question in the past perfect continuous: Had they been playing…?
why.es: Una pregunta en pasado perfecto continuo: Had they been playing…?

Have.en: Have they been is a present perfect continuous question; the sentence is in the past (started).
Have.es: Have they been es una pregunta en presente perfecto continuo; la oración está en pasado (started).

Did.en: After Did you need the base verb (Did they play…?); “been playing” asks for had.
Did.es: Después de Did hace falta el verbo base (Did they play…?); «been playing» pide had.

examples: Had he been sleeping?
Had you been waiting long?

tr.en: Had they been playing long when it started to rain?
tr.es: ¿Habían estado jugando mucho tiempo cuando empezó a llover?

why.en: A number (three reports), a finished result: the simple past perfect, had written.
why.es: Un número (tres reportes), un resultado terminado: pasado perfecto simple, had written.

was writing.en: “Was writing” is an action at one moment; “by noon” asks for the result finished by then.
was writing.es: «Was writing» es una acción en un solo momento; «by noon» pide el resultado terminado para entonces.

writes.en: Writes is present and marks a habit; by noon asks for a finished result.
writes.es: Writes es presente y marca un hábito; by noon pide un resultado terminado.

examples: By six, he had finished two books.
By May, they had opened the shop.

tr.en: By noon, she had written three reports.
tr.es: Para el mediodía, ella había escrito tres informes.

items.sentence: He had been ___ for hours when the phone rang.

why.en: After had been comes verb-ing: had been sleeping.
why.es: Después de had been va verbo-ing: had been sleeping.

slept.en: “Slept” is a past form; after had been comes the -ing form (sleeping).
slept.es: «Slept» es una forma de pasado; después de had been va la forma -ing (sleeping).

sleep.en: The base verb after had been is incorrect; you need the -ing form (sleeping).
sleep.es: El verbo base después de had been es incorrecto; hace falta la forma -ing (sleeping).

examples: She had been reading for an hour.
We had been eating for ten minutes.

tr.en: He had been sleeping for hours when the phone rang.
tr.es: Él había estado durmiendo por horas cuando sonó el teléfono.

items.sentence: We had been living there ___ 2015 when we moved away.

why.en: 2015 is a starting point, so you need since: since 2015.
why.es: 2015 es un punto de inicio, por eso hace falta since: since 2015.

for.en: For goes before a duration (for ten years); 2015 is a starting point.
for.es: For va antes de una duración (for ten years); 2015 es un punto de inicio.

ago.en: Ago goes with the past simple and follows a duration (ten years ago); here the verb is in the past perfect continuous.
ago.es: Ago va con el pasado simple y sigue a una duración (ten years ago); aquí el verbo está en pasado perfecto continuo.

examples: She had been working here since May.
They had been waiting since noon.

tr.en: We had been living there since 2015 when we moved away.
tr.es: Habíamos estado viviendo ahí desde 2015 cuando nos mudamos.

items.sentence: They had been living here ___ ten years when she left.

why.en: Ten years is a duration, so you need for: for ten years.
why.es: Diez años es una duración, por eso hace falta for: for ten years.

since.en: Since needs a starting point (since 2010), not a duration.
since.es: Since pide un punto de inicio (since 2010), no una duración.

ago.en: Ago goes with the past simple (ten years ago); here it is had been living.
ago.es: Ago va con el pasado simple (ten years ago); aquí es had been living.

examples: He had been teaching for five years.
We had been married for a year.

tr.en: They had been living here for ten years when she left.
tr.es: Ellos habían estado viviendo aquí por diez años cuando ella se fue.

items.sentence: I had ___ her for years, so I said hello.

why.en: Know is a state verb with no continuous form: had known.
why.es: Know es un verbo de estado sin forma continua: had known.

been knowing.en: Know takes no -ing form, so “had been knowing” is incorrect.
been knowing.es: Know no lleva -ing, por eso «had been knowing» es incorrecto.

knowing.en: After had you need the participle (known), not the -ing form.
knowing.es: Después de had hace falta el participio (known), no la forma -ing.

examples: I had known him for years.
She had had that car for ten years.

tr.en: I had known her for years, so I said hello.
tr.es: La conocía desde hace años, así que la saludé.

items.sentence: I ___ there since morning when you called.

why.en: “Since morning” is a starting point before the call: had been waiting.
why.es: «Since morning» es un punto de inicio antes de la llamada: had been waiting.

was waiting.en: “Was waiting since” is a word-for-word copy of the Spanish “estaba esperando desde”; in English since asks for the past perfect continuous.
was waiting.es: «Was waiting since» es una copia palabra por palabra del «estaba esperando desde»; en inglés since pide el pasado perfecto continuo.

have been waiting.en: Have been waiting refers to the present; the sentence looks back from a moment in the past (called).
have been waiting.es: Have been waiting se refiere al presente; la oración mira atrás desde un momento del pasado (called).

examples: She had been sleeping since noon.
We had been working since six.

tr.en: I had been waiting there since morning when you called.
tr.es: Había estado esperando ahí desde la mañana cuando llamaste.

items.sentence: She hadn't ___ well, so she saw a doctor.

why.en: After hadn’t comes been + verb-ing: hadn’t been feeling.
why.es: Después de hadn’t va been + verbo-ing: hadn’t been feeling.

feeling.en: “Hadn’t feeling” is incomplete: after hadn’t you also need been.
feeling.es: «Hadn’t feeling» está incompleto: después de hadn’t también hace falta been.

been felt.en: “Been felt” would be a passive (it was felt); here you need the -ing form (been feeling).
been felt.es: «Been felt» sería una pasiva (fue sentido); aquí hace falta la forma -ing (been feeling).

examples: He hadn't been sleeping well.
They hadn't been working.

tr.en: She hadn't been feeling well, so she saw a doctor.
tr.es: Ella no se había estado sintiendo bien, así que vio a un médico.

items.sentence: He was angry because he ___ for an hour.

why.en: The reason for his anger is the earlier waiting for an hour: had been waiting.
why.es: La razón de su enojo es la espera anterior de una hora: had been waiting.

has been waiting.en: Has been waiting refers to the present; the sentence is in the past (was angry).
has been waiting.es: Has been waiting se refiere al presente; la oración está en pasado (was angry).

waits.en: Waits is present and a habit; the sentence is in the past (was angry).
waits.es: Waits es presente y un hábito; la oración está en pasado (was angry).

examples: She was tired because she had been working.
They were wet because they had been walking.

tr.en: He was angry because he had been waiting for an hour.
tr.es: Él estaba enojado porque había estado esperando por una hora.

items.sentence: The kids were tired when we got home. They ___ outside since lunch.

why.en: “Since lunch” is a starting point before we got home: had been playing.
why.es: «Since lunch» es un punto de inicio antes de llegar a casa: had been playing.

were playing.en: Since does not go with the past continuous; time lasting up to getting home needs had been playing.
were playing.es: Since no va con el pasado continuo; el tiempo que dura hasta llegar a casa necesita had been playing.

have been playing.en: Have been playing refers to the present; the sentence is in the past (were tired).
have been playing.es: Have been playing se refiere al presente; la oración está en pasado (were tired).

examples: He had been walking since six.
We had been talking since lunch.

tr.en: The kids were tired when we got home. They had been playing outside since lunch.
tr.es: Los niños estaban cansados cuando llegamos a casa. Habían estado jugando afuera desde el almuerzo.

items.sentence: He ___ for long when the boss arrived.

why.en: An action that had not lasted long up to the arrival: hadn’t been working.
why.es: Una acción que no había durado mucho hasta la llegada: hadn’t been working.

doesn't work.en: Doesn’t work is present; the sentence looks back to a past point (arrived).
doesn't work.es: Doesn’t work es presente; la oración mira atrás a un punto del pasado (arrived).

hasn't been working.en: Hasn’t been working refers to the present; the sentence is in the past (arrived).
hasn't been working.es: Hasn’t been working se refiere al presente; la oración está en pasado (arrived).

examples: She hadn't been sleeping long.
We hadn't been waiting long.

tr.en: He hadn't been working for long when the boss arrived.
tr.es: Él no había estado trabajando por mucho tiempo cuando llegó el jefe.

items.sentence: Last year she told me she ___ for a job for months.

why.en: Told puts the sentence in the past, and the looking lasted for months before the telling: had been looking.
why.es: Told pone la oración en pasado, y la búsqueda duró meses antes de decirlo: had been looking.

is looking.en: Is looking is present; last year and told point to the past (had been looking).
is looking.es: Is looking es presente; last year y told señalan el pasado (had been looking).

will be looking.en: Will be looking refers to the future; the sentence is a past report (told).
will be looking.es: Will be looking se refiere al futuro; la oración es un reporte pasado (told).

examples: He said he had been waiting.
They said they had been working.

tr.en: Last year she told me she had been looking for a job for months.
tr.es: El año pasado ella me dijo que había estado buscando trabajo por meses.

items.sentence: Her eyes were sore because she ___ at the screen since morning.

why.en: “Since morning” is a starting point before the soreness: had been looking.
why.es: «Since morning» es un punto de inicio antes del dolor: had been looking.

looked.en: “Looked since morning” is incorrect; since needs a continuous perfect form.
looked.es: «Looked since morning» es incorrecto; since necesita una forma perfecta continua.

was looking.en: Since does not go with the past continuous; you need had been looking.
was looking.es: Since no va con el pasado continuo; hace falta had been looking.

examples: She had been reading since lunch.
He had been working since six.

tr.en: Her eyes were sore because she had been looking at the screen since morning.
tr.es: Le dolían los ojos porque había estado mirando la pantalla desde la mañana.

text.es: pasado perfecto: un resultado terminado

wrong.en: “Been waiting” describes a process and a duration (for two hours), not a finished result.
wrong.es: «Been waiting» describe un proceso y una duración (for two hours), no un resultado terminado.

text.en: past perfect continuous: a process lasting up to a point in the past
text.es: pasado perfecto continuo: un proceso que dura hasta un punto del pasado

text.en: past continuous: an action at one moment
text.es: pasado continuo: una acción en un solo momento

items.es: By noon, she had written three reports.

tr.es: Para el mediodía, había escrito tres reportes.

text.en: past perfect continuous: the length of the process
text.es: pasado perfecto continuo: la duración del proceso

wrong.en: Here a number is given (three reports), so the finished result takes the simple past perfect.
wrong.es: Aquí se da un número (three reports), por eso el resultado terminado va con el pasado perfecto simple.

text.es: pasado perfecto: un número, un resultado terminado

text.es: pasado simple: un hecho terminado

tr.es: La conocía desde hacía años.

text.es: pasado perfecto continuo: una duración

wrong.en: Know is a state verb with no continuous form even though there is a duration (for years).
wrong.es: Know es un verbo de estado sin forma continua aunque haya una duración (for years).

text.en: past perfect: know is a state verb
text.es: pasado perfecto: know es un verbo de estado

text.en: past simple: a finished period
text.es: pasado simple: un periodo terminado

wrong.en: Had known describes a state up to an earlier point in the past; the past simple does not show the other point.
wrong.es: Had known describe un estado hasta un punto anterior del pasado; el pasado simple no muestra el otro punto.

tr.en: How long had you been driving when the car stopped?
tr.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevabas manejando cuando se paró el carro?

text.en: present perfect continuous: time up to now
text.es: presente perfecto continuo: tiempo hasta ahora

wrong.en: The question looks back from a point in the past (stopped), not from now; that is why had been.
wrong.es: La pregunta mira atrás desde un punto del pasado (stopped), no desde ahora; por eso had been.

text.en: past perfect continuous: asks about the length up to a point in the past
text.es: pasado perfecto continuo: pregunta por la duración hasta un punto del pasado

text.en: past simple: a finished time
text.es: pasado simple: un tiempo terminado

wrong.en: “How long did you drive?” would ask about the whole length of the drive; had been driving asks about the time up to the stop.
wrong.es: «How long did you drive?» preguntaría por toda la duración del viaje; had been driving pregunta por el tiempo hasta la parada.

text.es: for + una duración
